headline: Funding flows. Tests stumble. Partnerships form.
deck: This week saw fresh capital in space, but not all tests hit the mark.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in Series C funding, valuing the company at $1.6 billion. This round underscores the demand for co-orbital security solutions as the Department of Defense leans into satellite defense. Investors are clearly betting on the notion that protecting space assets is the new frontier.
stories.soWhat: If the DoD is the headline, True Anomaly might just be the headline act.

stories.head: Sierra Space’s Dream Chaser variant clears review
stories.body: Sierra Space announced that its Dream Chaser DoD variant has passed a critical design review, a milestone that suggests the company is on track for future government contracts. The Dream Chaser's design aims to provide cargo and crew transportation, which could be a game-changer for military logistics in space.
stories.soWhat: Let’s just hope it doesn’t end up like the sequel no one asked for.

stories.head: Space Force awards TrustPoint $4M for navigation
stories.body: The Space Force has awarded TrustPoint a $4 million contract to develop a C-band navigation system aimed at enhancing low Earth orbit navigation. This contract is part of a broader push to create alternatives to GPS, which has become a bit like diet soda—always trying to find its moment in the spotlight.
stories.soWhat: If GPS is the gold standard, TrustPoint is just trying to be the next best alternative.

watchlist.title: Watch for more co-orbital funding rounds
watchlist.body: As True Anomaly leads the charge, expect other players in co-orbital security to seek capital, especially with rising geopolitical tensions.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's next steps post-review
watchlist.body: With the Dream Chaser variant cleared, watch for announcements on partnerships or contracts that could follow, especially with the DoD.

watchlist.title: TrustPoint's navigation system progress
watchlist.body: Keep an eye on TrustPoint's development timeline; if they can deliver on this contract, it could set the stage for more lucrative deals.

watchlist.title: Potential IPOs in defense-tech
watchlist.body: As the defense-tech IPO window creaks open, companies like Anduril may be looking to capitalize, so prepare for valuation gymnastics.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.

tickers.note: Virgin Galactic continues to hover around $5, with no clear flight plan in sight.
Palantir's $480M extension on the TITAN program shows that software is still a lucrative space play.
Aerojet Rocketdyne is bouncing back this week, but investors should still check the launch schedule.
Lockheed Martin's stock remains steady as defense budgets increase, but watch for any contract delays.
